name: Rifle Apartments
headline: Evergreen Real Estate Group built Rifle Apartments, 60 family apartments for households at 30% to 80% AMI in three three-story buildings at 115, 123 and 131 Park Avenue in downtown Rifle, with a 2023 Round One 9% award; it held a grand opening on 2026-04-17 and was reported 95% leased.
why_it_matters: It is a finished rural Western Slope 9% deal that won on its second try after moving to a larger site with surface parking, and that stacked Division of Housing gap and Transformational Housing loans, Colorado Clean Energy Fund and Capital Magnet Fund money with 14 Garfield County Housing Authority project-based vouchers.

status.label: Open: grand opening 2026-04-17; 95% leased
status.detail: Evergreen broke ground on 2024-09-27 and announced completion with a grand opening on April 17 (2026, inferred from the 2026-04-27 report); Mile High CRE and ColoradoBiz reported the property 95% leased. Completion slipped from the fall 2025 target. The CHFA placed-in-service date is not public.

next_step: Watch for CHFA's placed-in-service record and stabilized occupancy reports.

key_numbers.meaning: All income-restricted at 30% to 80% AMI; 14 units carry Garfield County Housing Authority project-based vouchers.
About $14.5M over 10 years (inferred); Evergreen said it raised $12.3M of equity. Equal to the request.
$28,403,918 in the application, $29.2M in 2025; roughly $485,000 per unit (inferred).
$3M of gap funding plus a $5M Transformational Housing loan, per Evergreen in 2025.

facts.value: 115, 123 and 131 Park Avenue, Rifle (CHFA lists it as Highway 6 & Access Road, Rifle 81650)

Vacant 4.7-acre parcel along Rifle Creek, the largest vacant parcel in the Central Business District (Creekside Neighborhood sub-district), zoned for multifamily; just west of the Brenden Rifle 7 Theaters and north of U.S. Highway 6
Three three-story walk-up buildings; brick, metal, stone, wood and fiber cement cladding; all-electric; about an acre of green space with a playground; 115 free parking spaces with EV-ready charging

background.text: Evergreen's 2022 Round One application proposed a 50-unit, four-story elevator building with underground parking and 10 market-rate units at 139 Railroad Avenue; it was not funded, and the developer said CHFA and the city were concerned about the cost of structured parking and lack of green space, which led to the move to the larger Park Avenue site.

Rifle City Council reviewed the revised 60-unit plan at a workshop on 2023-01-04, where Evergreen asked for a $600,000 city match and the Garfield County Housing Authority said it would reserve 14 project-based vouchers if the project broke ground.

The project is the first family LIHTC property built in Rifle since 2002, per the application; the two older family LIHTC properties in Rifle (Eagles Nest and White River Village) reported no vacancies and waitlists.
The application said only a site plan review with a publicly noticed Planning Commission hearing remained before construction documents and a building permit.
The city secured state funding to improve Park Avenue; by April 2026 the Park Avenue extension was complete and construction had begun on the Park Avenue bridge.

Timeline slippage: the January 2023 plan aimed for a June 2024 groundbreaking and December 2025 opening; groundbreaking came on 2024-09-27 with completion set for fall 2025, and the grand opening was held in April 2026.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award description gives the income mix as 14 units at 30% AMI, 18 at 50%, 8 at 60%, 10 at 70% and 10 at 80%, while preliminary documents reported in January 2023 showed 14 at 30%, 12 at 50%, 18 at 60%, 8 at 70% and 8 at 80%.
The application put total development cost at $28,403,918, while Evergreen gave $29.2 million in 2025 and about $29 million at groundbreaking.

The application cited a $5,410,000 CHFA permanent loan and a $510,000 Impact Development Fund loan, while Evergreen's 2025 account lists a $3 million CHFA permanent loan and $1 million from Impact Development Fund.
